title: tools/clean_test_db.py and tests/integration/helpers.zig resetTestData() reference table names dropped/renamed years ago (process_events, event_store, dlq)
summary: Discovered while triaging the ~109 pre-existing zig build test-integration failures found during the ISS-0076 (GitHub #335) fix verification. tools/clean_test_db.py's TABLES list and tests/integration/helpers.zig's resetTestData() both hard-code table names process_events, event_store, and dlq for best-effort TRUNCATE/DELETE cleanup before/between test runs. None of these three table names exist anywhere in the current schema (public or any tenant schema) in the live bpm_test database -- confirmed via direct pg_tables query. The current names are events (not event_store) and dead_letter_items (not dlq, renamed by migrations/GBL-073_tnt01_drop_legacy_public_business_tables.sql per its own header comment); process_events does not correspond to any current table at all. Every integration test that goes through TestHarness.init() or clean_test_db.py therefore logs a POSTGRES ERROR 42P01 (relation does not exist) three times per invocation. The errors are individually caught and treated as best-effort/non-fatal (truncateTableBestEffort() swallows undefined_table), so this alone does not cause test failures, but it is pure log noise on every single integration test run and it means the CASCADE truncation these calls were meant to perform for the real events/dead_letter_items tables never actually happens (a table name typo is silently swallowed the same way a genuinely-missing table would be, so cleanup coverage is quietly incomplete).

root_cause.details: migrations/GBL-073_tnt01_drop_legacy_public_business_tables.sql and earlier rename migrations (072_tnt01_rename_legacy_tables.sql) renamed/dropped legacy table names as part of the TNT-01 schema-per-tenant migration, but tools/clean_test_db.py's TABLES list and helpers.zig's resetTestData() were never updated to match. Both files hard-code table names as plain strings with no validation against the live schema, so a rename anywhere in the migration history silently desyncs these lists with no compile-time or test-time signal -- the best-effort error handling that exists specifically to tolerate 'partial migration states' also perfectly hides permanent stale references.

occurrences.context: Discovered while running a git-stash baseline comparison of zig build test-integration to confirm the ISS-0076 fix introduced no regressions; found ~109 pre-existing failures/noisy-errors unrelated to ISS-0076, of which this stale-table-name noise is one of three identified independent causes.

prevention: Add a CI check (or a zig build step) that queries live schema_migrations-derived table names and fails if any string literal table name in tools/clean_test_db.py or helpers.zig's resetTestData()/truncateTableBestEffort() calls does not exist in the current public or tenant_default schema.
When a migration renames or drops a table, grep tools/ and tests/integration/helpers.zig for the old name as part of that migration's own change, not as a separate later cleanup.
